intro: Configuration values often arrive as text. Treating any nonempty string as true turns the literal false into a dangerous configuration error.
task: Convert explicit true/false/yes/no/1/0 strings after trimming and case normalization.
requirements: values is a sequence of strings. Strip whitespace and lowercase each; true, yes, 1 map to True and false, no, 0 map to False. Reject any other token. Return a bool list aligned to input.
Sequence inputs are Python lists or tuples of at most 1000 items. Text inputs contain valid Unicode scalar characters and at most 10000 characters.
Return the documented Python output types and preserve all caller inputs. Raise ValueError for invalid inputs unless the task explicitly reports a record-level rejection.

hints.title: Trace one record
hints.body: Use an explicit lookup table rather than Python truthiness.

hints.title: Handle the boundary
hints.body: The nonempty string false is truthy in Python; parsing must inspect its contents.

explanation: Configuration values often arrive as text. Treating any nonempty string as true turns the literal false into a dangerous configuration error.
A small accepted vocabulary makes this conversion auditable. Unknown values are rejected rather than guessed, which helps callers catch misspellings early.
